name: Tiffany Koyama Lane

bio.statement: The City of Portland says Koyama Lane was elected District 3 city councilor in November 2024 and began her term in January 2025.
bio.excerpt: Elected as City Councilor for District 3 in November 2024 and began their term of office in January 2025.

bio.statement: Koyama Lane's City of Portland page describes her as an award-winning educator, fourth-generation Japanese American, mom and community organizer.
bio.excerpt: She is an award-winning educator, fourth‑generation Japanese American, mom, and community organizer

bio.statement: The Portland Mercury reports Koyama Lane taught at Sunnyside Environmental School before running for council.
bio.excerpt: Prior to her City Council run, Koyama Lane was a teacher at Sunnyside Environmental School.

positions.statement: OPB reports Koyama Lane has spent her two years on council pushing for traffic safety and equity programs.
positions.excerpt: Koyama Lane has spent her two years in City Hall pushing for traffic safety, equity programs

positions.statement: The Portland Mercury reports Koyama Lane won't vote for city funding for the project unless the Trail Blazers ownership group contributes.
positions.excerpt: won’t vote to approve any city funding for the project if the Trail Blazers ownership group doesn’t chip in

positions.statement: In a Portland Tribune Q&A, Koyama Lane says corporations that benefit from Portland's workforce should pay their fair share.
positions.excerpt: We also need to make sure that corporations that benefit from our amazing workforce pay their fair share

positions.statement: In a Portland Tribune Q&A, Koyama Lane says she consistently hears worries about affordability and cuts to public goods.
positions.excerpt: Affordability is a worry I hear consistently from Portlanders, as are the massive cuts to our public goods.

collection_notes: Steps run identically for all 21 District 3 candidates: (1) county Military & Overseas Online Voters' Guide statement PDF (with the full and large-print county pamphlets tried where the statement PDF was a scan; the pamphlet's candidate index marks candidates who filed no statement) plus the City Auditor's AUD-120 candidate filing form linked from portland.gov's 2026 city candidates page; (2) portland.gov/council roster and councilor page for incumbents; (3) campaign domain only as printed in the pamphlet statement or filing form; (4) one general WebSearch; (5) three fixed allowed-domain WebSearch groups (opb.org+oregoncapitalchronicle.com+wweek.com+ballotpedia.org; kgw.com+koin.com+kptv.com+katu.com; portlandmercury.com+vote411.org+pamplinmedia.com+portlandtribune.com) because the search proxy rejects oregonlive.com and apnews.com; (6) the three articles that cover the whole District 3 field: OPB 'What to know about Portland's District 3 council race' (2026-10-07), Portland Mercury 'Meet the Candidates For City Council District 3' (2026-09-09) and Portland Tribune 'Meet the Portland City Council District 3 candidates' (2026-10-13; Q&A — the Tribune says Sollitt, Pham, Parker, McCormick, Kelly and Frankenstein did not respond and Tucker withdrew). Multi-winner race: OPB states three council seats are available in District 3. Excerpts come through a summarizing fetch tool that limits verbatim quotes to ~125 characters, so some are fragments. Ballot name/order match inventory.json and the county Ballot Content RCV report. Incumbent per portland.gov/council (listed under District 3).
